-5wpm-gesOY.summary: Tom Scott explains for Computerphile why handling time and timezones in code is so hard, walking through a simple web app that computes how long ago something happened. It covers the quirks of timezones and calendars and ends in an exasperated rant.
-5wpm-gesOY.why: It is the go-to funny, accessible explanation of why you should never implement datetime handling yourself, linked in nearly every timezone thread.

-6BsiVyC1kM.summary: Rich Hickey's JaxConf 2012 keynote examines what values are and why immutable values matter as information systems grow more complex and data gets bigger. It contrasts places with values and builds the case for immutability.
-6BsiVyC1kM.why: HN commenters cite it as the talk that convinced them of immutability and functional programming.

-J_xL4IGhJA.summary: The first lecture of MIT's 6.001 (SICP) with Abelson and Sussman, giving an overview of the course and an introduction to Lisp. It argues that computer science is about managing complexity and abstraction, not computers.
-J_xL4IGhJA.why: HN people recommend the SICP lectures as a deeper, livelier route into the book and a formative course even for seasoned programmers.

-zRN7XLCRhc.summary: Bryan Cantrill's LISA11 talk on how illumos arose after Oracle closed OpenSolaris. It covers the history of Sun, ZFS, DTrace and Zones, and the diaspora of kernel engineers, with a famous rant about Oracle and Larry Ellison.
-zRN7XLCRhc.why: HN points to it as the definitive, entertaining account of Sun's fate under Oracle, and quotes its Ellison lawnmower advice whenever Oracle behaves badly.

-k3mVnRlQLU.summary: Numberphile visits Cliff Stoll, the man behind ACME Klein Bottles, and sees how he stores a thousand glass Klein bottles in a crawlspace under his house. A remote-controlled forklift fetches them.
-k3mVnRlQLU.why: HN commenters love Cliff Stoll's earnest, playful personality and point to this as a delightful look at his unusual warehouse.

-6rWqJhDv7M.summary: Physicist Carlo Rovelli gives a public lecture at the Royal Institution on how our understanding of time has changed, from Boltzmann and Einstein to quantum theory and loop quantum gravity. He blends physics, philosophy and art to argue that time is stranger than everyday intuition suggests.
-6rWqJhDv7M.why: HN commenters point to it as a lucid, general-audience lecture that shows how wrong common conceptions of time are, often in threads on entropy and the arrow of time.

-HFwok9SlQQ.summary: Adam Conover's talk at a millennial marketing conference argues that generations are an unscientific, condescending idea and that millennials do not exist as a real category. The description notes that researcher Jean Twenge later said he misrepresented some of her work.
-HFwok9SlQQ.why: HN commenters cite it when arguing that generational labels are marketing inventions used to belittle groups.

-fny99f8amM.summary: Adam Curtis's 2016 BBC documentary HyperNormalisation, about 160 minutes long. It cuts together roughly forty years of politics, finance and technology to argue that people have retreated into a simplified fake world.
-fny99f8amM.why: Strongly and repeatedly recommended as a visually distinctive documentary and a guide to postmodern ideas on politics, truth and technology.

-VsmF9m_Nt8.summary: A 1972 song by Adriano Celentano whose lyrics are nonsense syllables designed to sound like American English to non-English speakers. It is a rock and rap-flavored novelty track with a video.
-VsmF9m_Nt8.why: It comes up whenever threads touch on fake languages, accents, or gibberish that sounds plausible, and commenters like sharing it with people who haven't heard it.

-4Yp3j_jk8Q.summary: Leslie Lamport argues that programmers, like architects, should write rigorous specifications before coding, especially for concurrent and distributed systems. The talk introduces the case for writing specs (the TLA+ mindset) as a way of thinking above the code.
-4Yp3j_jk8Q.why: HN points people to it as Lamport's own case for thinking and writing a spec before coding, and as an entry point to TLA+.

-k-V3ESHcfA.summary: Mark Rober makes a plant-based burger for Bill Gates and explains why meat production strains the environment. Gates also appears and discusses his worry about steel and cement.
-k-V3ESHcfA.why: HN commenters cite it as a short, accessible overview of the climate and water case for plant-based meat.

-FENubmZGj8.summary: Law professor James Duane explains why you should not talk to the police even if you are innocent, drawing on case histories of wrongful convictions. It is a short version of the argument in his book on the right to remain silent.
-FENubmZGj8.why: HN commenters send it to anyone who thinks innocent people have nothing to fear from answering police questions.

-Ht4qiDRZE8.summary: Luis von Ahn, creator of CAPTCHA and reCAPTCHA, explains how small contributions from many people online can digitize books. He then introduces Duolingo as a way to translate the web while people learn languages.
-Ht4qiDRZE8.why: HN commenters recommend it as the clearest account of human computation and games with a purpose, straight from the inventor.

-iCIZQX9i1A.summary: Miniminuteman begins a long, humorous point-by-point debunking of Graham Hancock's Netflix series Ancient Apocalypse and its claims of a lost ice-age civilization. It is part one of a multi-part critique.
-iCIZQX9i1A.why: HN points people to it as an entertaining, thorough takedown of Hancock's pseudoarchaeology whenever his claims come up.

-4EDhdAHrOg.summary: A two-minute comedy sketch in which a woman describes her problems while a visible nail sticks out of her head, and her partner keeps trying to fix it instead of listening. It dramatizes the gap between wanting empathy and being offered solutions.
-4EDhdAHrOg.why: HN commenters link it as the quickest memorable illustration of listening versus problem-solving, and as shorthand in threads on empathy and support.

-4FXLQoLDBA.summary: An animated simulation comparing single-winner voting methods such as plurality, instant runoff and STAR. Colored regions show which candidate wins as a randomized electorate shifts across a two-dimensional political space, building on Ka-Ping Yee's earlier diagrams.
-4FXLQoLDBA.why: HN commenters cite it in voting-reform threads as a visual argument that cardinal systems (STAR, approval) beat plurality and ranked-choice voting.

-R-eqJDQ2nU.summary: Rhonda Patrick interviews Salk Institute researcher Satchidananda Panda about circadian rhythms and the timing of food. They cover time-restricted feeding and its links to obesity, muscle mass, heart health, and light exposure.
-R-eqJDQ2nU.why: Recommended in threads on fasting and nutrition as a deep dive from the lead researcher on time-restricted eating.

-ZxPhDC-r3w.summary: Intrinsic Gravity is a real-time demoscene production by Still, made with the Tooll tool for Under Construction 2014. It is a black-and-white op-art animation with a soundtrack by hoffman.
-ZxPhDC-r3w.why: HN people hold it up as a standout modern demo, praising its scene transitions and how it looks on 3D displays.

-whuXHSL1Pg.summary: Coffeezilla gives a comprehensive history of Tether, the stablecoin issued by a company controlled by the owners of Bitfinex. He lays out accusations that it is not fully backed.
-whuXHSL1Pg.why: HN commenters recommend it as the best single, entertaining overview of Tether's dubious history, and cite it when arguing Tether lacks real USD backing.

-I_jE0l7sYQ.summary: Erlang co-creator Joe Armstrong's Code BEAM SF 2018 keynote revisits good ideas from the history of computing that were dropped, and asks which should be revived. It also touches on Erlang and Elixir.
-I_jE0l7sYQ.why: HN people recommend it as a reading list of historical CS ideas worth knowing, and as a favorite among Armstrong's talks, especially after his death.

-Ln-8QM8KhQ.summary: Wes Bos breaks down the techniques behind the McMaster-Carr website's speed: server-rendered HTML, prefetching, CDN and service worker caching, preloading, critical CSS and fixed-size images. He also notes its old-school jQuery and YUI JavaScript.
-Ln-8QM8KhQ.why: HN points to it as the clearest frontend explanation of why McMaster-Carr feels so snappy, often contrasted with slow modern UIs.

-f-CFQxaUY4.summary: Rhonda Patrick interviews Dr. Bill Harris, co-inventor of the Omega-3 Index and author of more than 300 papers on fatty acids. They cover EPA and DHA dosing, fish oil studies such as REDUCE-IT, and how omega-3 levels relate to health and longevity.
-f-CFQxaUY4.why: HN commenters point to it as a researcher-led answer on omega-3 dosing, with the takeaway that most people take too little.

-suTmUX4Vbk.summary: America's Test Kitchen tests eight carbon-steel skillets to find the best one, asking whether a single pan can replace stainless, cast iron and nonstick. It names a winner and covers how the pans perform.
-suTmUX4Vbk.why: HN people link it as a solid explainer and review of carbon steel pans, and for seasoning guidance.

-2ZTmuX3cog.summary: Jason Scott of Archive Team describes how a loose band of volunteers rushes to copy sites like Geocities, Friendster and Yahoo Video before their owners delete them. The talk covers the tactics they use and the argument that this data is history worth saving.
-2ZTmuX3cog.why: HN points to it whenever a company shuts down a service and wipes user content, as an entertaining case for digital preservation.

-bYAQ-ZZtEU.summary: Investigative journalist Sharyl Attkisson explains how astroturf, fake grassroots campaigns funded by corporate or political interests, manipulates media messages. The TEDx talk is about 11 minutes.
-bYAQ-ZZtEU.why: HN commenters recommend it as an introduction to shills, astroturfing and lobbyist influence on media, especially in threads about fake news and online forums.

-cEn_83zRFw.summary: DHH's opening keynote at Rails World 2024 in Toronto, where Rails 8 beta shipped. It covers built-in authentication, Propshaft, Solid Cache, Solid Queue, Solid Cable, Kamal 2 and Thruster, pitching the One Person Framework that needs no PaaS.
-cEn_83zRFw.why: HN commenters point to it as a primer on modern Rails and as a rebuttal to cloud 'learned helplessness', worth watching even by non-Ruby developers.

-qCKR6wy94U.summary: John Oliver's second Last Week Tonight segment on the opioid epidemic, covering the role of large companies in driving it. It touches on Purdue Pharma and the Sackler family.
-qCKR6wy94U.why: Commenters cite it, with Oliver's other two opioid segments, as a well-researched case against pharma marketing and the Purdue settlements.

-8nqnOcoLqE.summary: Permaculture instructor Andrew Millison visits the village of Garavadi in Maharashtra, India, which took part in the Paani Foundation's Water Cup competition. It shows the water harvesting structures the villagers built in 45 days and how they restored groundwater and the local economy.
-8nqnOcoLqE.why: HN commenters point to it as a hopeful example of land and water management restoring landscapes and livelihoods at village scale.

-EA2FQXs4dw.summary: Linus Tech Tips reviews the Looking Glass 8K holographic display, a glasses-free 3D monitor. The video shows the display in action and explains how it works.
-EA2FQXs4dw.why: HN uses it as a reasonably detailed overview of Looking Glass tech, including a segment showing the pixel mapping behind the 3D effect.

-QWHkcCP3tA.summary: Gary Vaynerchuk's keynote at RailsConf 2010 in Baltimore. The Wine Library TV founder talks about building a business and audience through genuine effort and caring about customers.
-QWHkcCP3tA.why: HN commenters recommend it as an energetic, unscripted talk on creating for the long term and hustling.

-gGLvg0n-uY.summary: A fan-made Metal Gear Solid 2 codec call using AI voice synthesis, in which the Colonel warns Raiden about using AI to censor the internet and enforce digital ID. It riffs on the game's 'Selection for Societal Sanity' conversation.
-gGLvg0n-uY.why: HN users post it as a meme or satirical comment in threads about AI regulation, age verification and online identity.

-i6wvix6buI.summary: Kyle Drake of Neocities explains the bandwidth pricing pitfalls of the big cloud providers. He describes how to run high-volume, bandwidth-heavy infrastructure far more cheaply, including through co-location.
-i6wvix6buI.why: HN recommends it whenever cloud egress costs come up, since it gives concrete numbers on real bandwidth costs versus cloud pricing.

-pKR212H5vQ.summary: Tracy Young, a former construction engineer and cofounder of PlanGrid, speaks at the 2015 Y Combinator Female Founders Conference. She talks about building software for construction superintendents and about customer success.
-pKR212H5vQ.why: HN recommends it as a strong founder talk that shows how formidable and practical Young is, with advice delivered through a beaver metaphor.

-EVqrDlAqYo.summary: Lex Fridman interviews Jeff Hawkins, founder of Numenta and author of On Intelligence, about the Thousand Brains Theory and reverse-engineering the neocortex. They also cover Hierarchical Temporal Memory and brain-inspired AI architectures.
-EVqrDlAqYo.why: HN people send others here to hear Hawkins explain his theory in his own words, including reference frames and the old versus new brain.

-Im4YAMWK74.summary: A video essay from lawyer-turned-YouTuber Moon Channel on the South Korean gender war, tracing its historical roots and modern origins through the lens of a gacha game controversy. It is the first part of a two-part series.
-Im4YAMWK74.why: HN commenters recommend it, along with its sequel, as an enlightening explanation of the economic and cultural roots of gender friction in South Korea.

-J8YyfrSwTk.summary: Yaron Minsky of Jane Street gave this talk to Harvard's OCaml-based CS51 class in 2010. It collects advice on being an effective ML programmer in an industrial setting.
-J8YyfrSwTk.why: It is the go-to source for the idea of making illegal states unrepresentable through types, with the key moment at 28:02.

-Qph8BNrnLY.summary: Jeri Ellsworth demonstrates a PMOS transistor she fabricated herself in a home chip lab. She shows some of its electrical characteristics.
-Qph8BNrnLY.why: HN likes Ellsworth as a hardware tinkerer, and cites the video as proof that transistors can be made with low-tech, DIY fabrication.

-bpX8YvNg6Y.summary: Zoz's DEF CON 23 talk explores practical, often explosive ways to destroy data and hard drives quickly. It tests methods such as thermite and other physical techniques for rapid destruction.
-bpX8YvNg6Y.why: HN points to it whenever hard drive destruction or fast physical data wiping comes up, as an empirical test of what actually works.

-7qT_38iRSc.summary: Psychologist Robert Epstein presents a Stanford EE380 colloquium on how internet algorithms such as search rankings can manipulate opinions, purchases and votes at massive scale. He also describes a new monitoring system for tracking such influence.
-7qT_38iRSc.why: Cited in threads about search bias, election influence and big-tech data practices as the most comprehensive video of Epstein's research.

-C-JoyNuQJs.summary: Douglas Crockford tells how JSON was discovered rather than invented, and how its simplicity made it a dominant data interchange format. He also covers surrounding history such as earlier Netscape usage and the 'Good, not Evil' license story.
-C-JoyNuQJs.why: HN commenters cite it as Crockford's first-hand account of JSON's origins and of the no-evil license anecdote.

-DVyjdw4t9I.summary: A roughly three-hour Lex Fridman podcast conversation with Guido van Rossum, the creator of Python. Topics include Python's design, the GIL, asyncio, the future of programming and AI coding tools.
-DVyjdw4t9I.why: HN points to it for Guido's own views on the GIL, Python internals and using Copilot, especially in Python-related threads.

-DX3vJiqxm4.summary: Pete Hunt explains why React's virtual DOM was built, how it compares with databinding-style systems, and what it means for future browser technology. Recorded at FutureJS 2014 in Barcelona.
-DX3vJiqxm4.why: Commenters point to it as the clearest explanation of why re-rendering beats tracking data changes, and say it sold them on React.

-K11rY57K7k.summary: Go runtime contributor Dmitry Vyukov looks inside the Go scheduler, explaining how goroutines and channels are implemented. He covers the main scheduler components and overall operation, then goes into details such as preemption and stacks.
-K11rY57K7k.why: Recommended as a good watch on how Go's M:N:P scheduler works and why it was designed that way compared with alternative schemes.

-MTRxRO5SRA.summary: Sal Khan of Khan Academy argues that schools push students forward with gaps in their foundations, and that students should instead master concepts at their own pace. He compares it to building a house on an unfinished foundation.
-MTRxRO5SRA.why: HN commenters cite it when discussing how gaps in basic knowledge pile up and how mastery learning could fix that.

-NL76uQOpI0.summary: Mathologer shows a simple idea, the commutator, that lets anyone who can solve the first layer design their own full Rubik's cube solution. The same idea carries over to other symmetric twisty puzzles such as the Megaminx.
-NL76uQOpI0.why: Recommended as an accessible explanation of how Rubik's cube solving relates to group theory.

-QMHOsfjHq0.summary: A philosophy lecture by Professor Moeller on the philosophy of identity. It builds on a discussion of Abigail Thorn's video and covers authenticity, sincerity and how online profiles reshape identity.
-QMHOsfjHq0.why: Cited in threads on social media and online identity as a framework of sincerity, authenticity and profilicity.

-ZSli7QW4rg.summary: Donnie Berkholz of RedMonk gives a Monki Gras talk arguing that abusive, toxic contributors damage open source projects. He makes the case for removing them from communities.
-ZSli7QW4rg.why: Cited as the go-to evidence that rudeness drives contributors away and that toxic people must be removed from projects.

-ZXrJRpA0Jw.summary: Linus Tech Tips reviews the Dasung Paperlike E-Ink monitor, asking whether an e-paper display makes sense as a computer monitor. The video covers its slow refresh rate, eye-comfort claims and day-to-day usability.
-ZXrJRpA0Jw.why: HN commenters cite it as a realistic demonstration of E-Ink monitor refresh rates and how such displays feel in use.

-_aL9V0JsQQ.summary: Jeff Geerling interviews Raspberry Pi co-founder Eben Upton about the Pi shortage, the RP2040, RISC-V, the Sony investment and the origin of the name.
-_aL9V0JsQQ.why: HN recommends it to explain why Pi supply favored business customers during the shortage, straight from a founder.

-epPf7D8oMk.summary: Jeff Geerling looks at a Sharp NEC commercial display with a slot for a Raspberry Pi Compute Module. It is a large screen without built-in smart TV features or tracking.
-epPf7D8oMk.why: Brought up in smart TV complaint threads as a real-world 'dumb display' alternative.

-gPuH1yeZ08.summary: The 1997 novelty song by Komar and Melamid with composer Dave Soldier, built from survey results on what listeners dislike most in music. It features bagpipes, an opera singer rapping, and a children's choir urging shopping at Wal-Mart.
-gPuH1yeZ08.why: Cited in threads about taste and terrible music as a famously engineered 'worst song', mostly for its curiosity value.

-gYb5GUs0dM.summary: A short screen recording of the flight simulator Easter egg hidden in Excel 97, with the steps to trigger it. The uploader notes the mouse controls are hard to handle.
-gYb5GUs0dM.why: HN commenters link it as a fond example of elaborate hidden Easter eggs in old Microsoft Office.

-hCimLnIsDA.summary: A three-minute clip in which Douglas Crockford explains why he allowed the JSLint reference implementation to be used for evil. It recounts the license clause and how corporate lawyers reacted.
-hCimLnIsDA.why: Linked in licensing threads as a short, funny story about the 'no evil' clause and IBM's request for an exception.

-hxX_Q5CnaA.summary: A short 2009 video of Jeff Bezos talking about Amazon and Zappos. He discusses customer focus, invention and long-term thinking.
-hxX_Q5CnaA.why: HN commenters like his candid, authentic delivery and the lessons on customer obsession and thinking long term.

-opBifFfsMY.summary: Freya Holmer delivers a long critique of generative AI, arguing it degrades the internet by flooding it with machine-generated junk. The video grew out of her frustration finding reliable information about a technical file format.
-opBifFfsMY.why: HN people link it when discussing AI-generated spam clogging search results and the broader harm of generative AI to the web.

-q7ZVXOU3kM.summary: Urban explorers break into the Baikonur cosmodrome in Kazakhstan to film the abandoned Soviet Buran space shuttles. The video shows the decaying orbiters and the dangerous trip to reach them.
-q7ZVXOU3kM.why: Linked in space and Soviet-history threads as striking footage of the rotting Buran shuttles.

-t1_ffaFXao.summary: A roughly four-and-a-half-hour Lex Fridman podcast conversation with Stephen Wolfram about his Wolfram Physics Project and a fundamental theory of physics, computation, life and the universe.
-t1_ffaFXao.why: HN points to it as a detailed explanation of Wolfram's physics hypothesis, and for Wolfram's evident passion, though some find it long.

-dk3NOEgX7o.summary: A FRONTLINE documentary on whether efforts to fix plastic pollution made it worse. It looks at the battle over plastics and recycling and how little plastic is actually recycled.
-dk3NOEgX7o.why: HN recommends it as an eye-opener on how recycling was promoted by the plastics industry despite not working.

-jCwIsT0X8M.summary: Dan Worrall explains when higher sample rates help in recording and mixing, and when they do not. He goes into oversampling versus higher sample rates, and aliasing in distortion plugins.
-jCwIsT0X8M.why: Recommended as a clear explainer on Nyquist, aliasing and sample rate conversion artifacts.

-s5szfPYKY4.summary: A UCTV panel with endocrinologist Robert Lustig, dentist Cristen Kearns and health policy expert Laura Schmidt on how the US food system and sugar industry influence diet and health, including industry efforts to shape the science.
-s5szfPYKY4.why: HN cites it in threads on sugar, nutrition science and industry influence over health research.

-BLgS7m0W94.summary: A short Techquickie explainer on why laptop webcams are much worse than phone cameras. It covers sensor size, image processing, and the interface differences between laptops and phones, with input from a Logitech engineer.
-BLgS7m0W94.why: HN commenters link it when webcam quality comes up, as a quick rundown of why laptop webcams lag behind phones.

-BeTq99LqUo.summary: Styropyro tests an eBay laser tattoo removal device and finds it is a roughly million-watt pulsed laser, powerful enough to ignite air in the beam. He had bought it hoping to salvage an Nd:YAG laser cavity.
-BeTq99LqUo.why: HN mostly cites it as an example of the absurdly powerful lasers sold cheaply online, and a nod to the channel's DIY laser builds.

-E6vHCT0wpw.summary: Yuta, a Japanese YouTuber, explains whether Japanese speakers can read Chinese text. He shows how shared kanji let people guess meanings while the two languages remain completely different.
-E6vHCT0wpw.why: Cited in threads on writing systems and CJK characters as an entertaining test of how much Japanese people can understand of Chinese.

-JlxuQ7tPgQ.summary: A speculative-fiction video by Tom Scott, framed as coming from a future, about an AI called Earworm that enforces copyright so aggressively that humanity ends up forgetting a century of pop culture. It is animated and narrated as part of his series of videos from a future.
-JlxuQ7tPgQ.why: HN points to it in discussions of AI copyright enforcement and badly specified AI goals, and recommends it alongside his other fiction.

-KxjVlaLBmk.summary: A short demo from the Ishikawa Komuro Lab of a high-speed robot hand paired with a 1000fps vision system performing dexterous manipulation. It shows what very low-latency vision and actuation can do.
-KxjVlaLBmk.why: HN cites it as an example of what 1kHz vision and fast control loops enable, in threads about AI hardware and robotics.

-Rxvl3INKSg.summary: An ABC7 News Bay Area reporter rides in a driverless Waymo robotaxi through San Francisco and documents the trip, including a couple of awkward moments. It is a short TV news segment showing what a robotaxi ride is actually like.
-Rxvl3INKSg.why: Cited in self-driving threads as a firsthand look at robotaxi rides, mostly to point out its glitches and doubts about readiness.

-TKjwblp1XI.summary: A half-hour television special on the 2007 fiery collapse of a connector in the Bay Area's MacArthur Maze and its rebuilding in 26 days. It was produced for the Professional Engineers in California Government.
-TKjwblp1XI.why: HN cites it as proof that infrastructure can be rebuilt very fast when incentives and urgency line up.

-VrJ8XOwJzw.summary: A choral recording by Cappella Romana from the album Lost Voices of Hagia Sophia. It is part of a project recreating Byzantine chant using the acoustics of the Hagia Sophia.
-VrJ8XOwJzw.why: Cited as an example of the Hagia Sophia acoustic recreation project, where a choir performs with the building's measured impulse response.

-ZDZtBRTyeI.summary: A Vox explainer from the 2020 election series on why American public transit is so poor. It traces the effect of the interstate highway system on cities and the resulting car dependence.
-ZDZtBRTyeI.why: Linked in transit and infrastructure threads as a general explanation, with one commenter drawing the point that good transit depends on networks.

-ga41edXw3A.summary: The original Amiga Boing Ball demo, written at the Winter CES in January 1984 to show off the Amiga's hardware, with a bouncing, spinning checkered ball running while the system multitasked. It became the Amiga's unofficial emblem.
-ga41edXw3A.why: HN people recall it with nostalgia as an impressive feat for its era, used as an example of the Amiga's graphics ability.

-kFOXP026eE.summary: The first of Richard Feynman's 1964 Messenger Lectures at Cornell, 'The Character of Physical Law', covering the law of gravitation. Feynman traces the history from Kepler and Newton to the universality of the inverse-square law. The recording is an older one with weak audio.
-kFOXP026eE.why: Commenters cite it as a classic of physics lectures for laypeople that they watch and rewatch, though the audio quality is noted as poor.

-oB6DN5dYWo.summary: An English-subtitled German workplace safety film about forklift driver Klaus. It is campy and darkly comic, staging an escalating series of forklift accidents.
-oB6DN5dYWo.why: Mostly used as a joke reference whenever forklifts, safety or dying on the job come up, with one commenter calling it a funny and bloody case for warehouse safety.

-r2oaQWmqkk.summary: Mick West shows new night-vision reference footage indicating the Navy's supposed flying pyramid UFO is just an out-of-focus light, likely a plane near LAX, rendered triangular by bokeh. He identifies other lights as Jupiter and stars.
-r2oaQWmqkk.why: HN cites it as a concise debunking of a UFO case and an illustration of how a triangular aperture creates triangle UFOs.

-wu_pO5Z7Pk.summary: Tobias Engel's 31C3 talk shows how weaknesses in the SS7 telephone signaling network let companies and attackers locate, track and manipulate phones from anywhere in the world, with precision down to about 50 meters.
-wu_pO5Z7Pk.why: HN cites it as the foundational demonstration that SS7 is insecure, relevant to arguments about SMS-based two-factor authentication.

-xTaAHSFHUU.summary: A nutrition-science explainer reviewing the human evidence on whether seed oils cause inflammation. It looks at nine different seed oils, heated oils, and genetic variability, and compares omega-6 intake with saturated fat.
-xTaAHSFHUU.why: HN commenters link it as a compact review of human trials showing seed oils are not inflammatory, to counter popular claims.

-zt57TWkTF4.summary: Linus Tech Tips gives its 2020 breakdown of how the company earns money, including ads, sponsors, merch and affiliate links. It includes a pie chart of revenue sources.
-zt57TWkTF4.why: HN cites it as concrete data on how a big YouTube channel diversifies revenue and how little comes from AdSense.

--LTYRTKV_A.summary: A one-minute clip from Insider showing an Airbus airliner's wings flexing far more than most people expect during a wing load test. It is meant to reassure nervous flyers about turbulence.
--LTYRTKV_A.why: HN commenters link it to show how much stress airliner wings are designed to withstand, especially in turbulence and crash threads.

-2ml6sjk_8c.summary: A short amateur clip of a Tesla Model S on Autopilot failing to follow a lane shift in a construction zone and hitting a concrete barrier. The uploader uses it to argue against driverless trucks.
-2ml6sjk_8c.why: Cited as a concrete example of Autopilot's limits whenever threads debate self-driving safety and Tesla's claims.

-C_jPcUkVrM.summary: A short GoPro film of Uli Emanuele's wingsuit BASE jump through a roughly 2 meter wide cave opening, after three years of preparation. It follows his climb to the exit point and the flight itself, shot on a HERO2 camera.
-C_jPcUkVrM.why: HN commenters cite it as a striking example of humans doing extremely dangerous, precise things for fun.

-F-IHvF5OCA.summary: A short scene from the Amazon series Patriot in which a spy character gives a deadpan, jargon-filled lecture about pipes and nut plate spacing. It is a comedic bit of corporate-cover absurdity.
-F-IHvF5OCA.why: HN commenters cite it as the funny reference whenever someone gives an impenetrable technical presentation.

-KSryJXDpZo.summary: A one-minute clip from Frans de Waal's TED talk showing two capuchin monkeys given unequal rewards (cucumber versus grape) for the same task. The monkey receiving the lesser reward reacts with protest.
-KSryJXDpZo.why: HN uses it as shorthand for the innate human and primate sense of fairness in threads on pay, wealth and inequality.

-RJf2jYzs8A.summary: Ben Alpert of the React team talks at React.js Conf 2016 about where React is heading. He covers performance and stability work, challenges at Facebook, and opportunities such as bringing React Native ideas to the web.
-RJf2jYzs8A.why: HN points to it as a primary source for what the React team was actually working on, such as React Native for the web.

-VcWF8dIDj4.summary: Amateur footage of a Japanese coast guard boat riding up and over large tsunami waves after the March 2011 Tohoku earthquake. It is short and unedited.
-VcWF8dIDj4.why: Cited in threads about earthquakes and tsunami warnings as a visceral view of what a tsunami wave looks like at sea.

-VfYjPzj1Xw.summary: A short PBS NewsHour clip of Elon Musk making a gesture at the post-inauguration celebration in January 2025, which many described as a fascist salute. The report includes the remarks he made just before it.
-VfYjPzj1Xw.why: HN mostly uses it as a primary-source link in long political arguments about the gesture, not as something to recommend.

-XSC_UG5_kU.summary: A short comedic video in which a man poses as an Apple engineer talking about the 2016 MacBook Pro. It is a critique of the USB-C-only design.
-XSC_UG5_kU.why: HN mentions it mostly as a joke in threads about dongles and USB-C.

-bMzFDpfDwc.summary: A 60 Minutes segment on how German prosecutors and police go after online hate speech and insults, which are crimes there. It contrasts this with the broad First Amendment protection of online speech in the US.
-bMzFDpfDwc.why: HN mostly cites it in unrelated threads as evidence of European speech restrictions, and some commenters call it propaganda.

-ccNkksrfls.summary: A one-minute clip of Diego Maradona's 'Hand of God' goal against England at the 1986 World Cup. It is part of a ClassicEngland series of unforgettable moments.
-ccNkksrfls.why: HN uses it as footage of a famous officiating failure, linked in Maradona obituary and video-review threads.

-dAjCeMuXR0.summary: An NBC News clip from 2020 of Kamala Harris on whether she would take a Covid-19 vaccine. She says she would if doctors said it was safe but not if Donald Trump told her to.
-dAjCeMuXR0.why: HN uses it as a source for what Harris actually said, in arguments about vaccine politics.

-e1_QhJ1EhQ.summary: Boston Dynamics shows its humanoid robot Atlas picking up and manipulating objects, and altering the obstacle course to reach its goal. The clip demonstrates locomotion, sensing and athletic manipulation.
-e1_QhJ1EhQ.why: Cited as a benchmark for how capable robots already are when HN debates AI, humanoids and automation.

-i0hat7pdpk.summary: A Google I/O 2011 talk by Andrew Gerrand and Rob Pike on building and deploying a web application in Go. It argues that Go offers speed, reliability and simplicity together.
-i0hat7pdpk.why: HN commenters cite it as an early official Go talk, including Rob Pike's remarks that Go aims to be useful rather than theoretically exciting.

-lErGZZgUbY.summary: Linus Tech Tips covers Framework's newly announced devices, including its first desktop, with comments from Framework's CEO about the company's design decisions.
-lErGZZgUbY.why: Used as a source for the Framework CEO's explanation of why the desktop's memory could not be socketed or modular.

-yUafzOXHPE.summary: A two-minute scene from It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia in which Mac and Dennis discuss the unspoken implication of going out on a boat. It is the full scene, unedited.
-yUafzOXHPE.why: HN uses it as a joke reference when discussing coercion, implied threats and consent in power imbalances.

-zVgWpVXb64.summary: A one-minute clip from the 1992 film Sneakers in which characters defeat a voice-authentication system by splicing recorded phrases, ending on the line "My voice is my passport." It was posted to illustrate a post on government surveillance.
-zVgWpVXb64.why: HN invokes it as a joke or reference whenever voice cloning or voice authentication comes up.
